title: Cookie consent MVP: blocker, banner, regions, cookie policy
body:
## What

Build the cookie consent MVP that replaces Complianz and Complianz Terms & Conditions: hold back scripts and embeds that set cookies until visitors allow them, a theme-matched banner only where needed, and a cookie policy that keeps itself current.

## Why

Complianz needs a scan, a wizard and ongoing upkeep. This plugin should work when switched on: recognise known services in the page as it is sent, decide per visitor in the browser (page-cache safe), and ask only as strictly as each region needs. Legal defaults stay configurable and are not legal advice.

## Scope

- Service registry (categories, URL and inline patterns, cookies, privacy links) and an output-buffer blocker for scripts and iframes, with placeholders and a Load button for embeds.
- Consent feature: settings, region model from the browser time zone (opt-in for Europe, Quebec, unclear; opt-out elsewhere; GPC turns marketing off), Google Consent Mode v2 defaults and updates, WP Consent API, banner and Cookie settings dialog, footer menu link and button, `#cookie-settings` links, Complianz one-off import.
- Cookie policy feature: block and shortcode listing the site's detected cookies, plus privacy policy guide text.
- Docs: `docs/architecture.md`, README, readme.txt, changelogs, `AGENTS.md`, `DESIGN.md` front-end section; uninstall cleanup.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-services.php`, `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php` (new)
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php` (new)
- `includes/views/consent-banner.php`, `assets/js/spcc-head.js`, `assets/js/spcc.js`, `assets/css/spcc.css`, `assets/js/blocks.js` (new)
- `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-setup.php`, `uninstall.php`

Reference pattern: features as classes listed in `SEOProCookieConsent_Setup::FEATURES` (`STANDARDS.md`).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh --wp 6.2 --php 7.4` pass with no PHP messages.
- Browser checks on a test site: Europe time zone holds everything back until Accept/Save/Load; Reject after Accept reloads and stops scripts; US time zone loads with a notice; GPC turns marketing off; dialog keyboard and Escape behaviour; no JS errors.

title: Hold back scripts and iframes added after page load (lightboxes)
body:
## What

Hold back scripts and iframes added after page load (lightboxes, sliders, tabbed embeds, page builders that inject iframes from templates or JSON), not only those in the HTML as sent.

## Why

The output-buffer blocker (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`) only sees the initial HTML. A YouTube lightbox inserts its iframe on click and loads without consent.

## Files

- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: a `MutationObserver` (started before other scripts run) that checks added `script` and `iframe` elements against the service patterns sent in the config, and holds back matches the same way the server does (`type="text/plain"`, `data-spcc-src`, placeholder for iframes).
- Patterns for the browser: add them to the front config in `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php` (keep it small: hosts only).
- `docs/architecture.md` → Holding back.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Test site, Europe time zone: a page that inserts a YouTube iframe and a GA script with JS after load shows a placeholder and does not request either until allowed; no JS errors; no measurable delay on pages without matches.

### Files Scope

- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`
- `assets/js/spcc.js`
- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

Implementation integration: `spcc.js` owns banner discovery and release, so it must consume dynamic matches and restore held script sources. Use compact URL match fragments rather than broadening shared hosts (Google hosts also serve necessary security scripts); do not ship built-in inline-code signatures. The observer needs synchronous insertion/source guards because notification occurs after script execution or network dispatch. Preserve exclusions, Google advanced mode, and page-builder editor bypasses. User documentation and changelogs are required by STANDARDS.md. PR #20 touches the consent feature and documentation for settings, but does not implement dynamic blocking; keep edits localized to config/head activation.

title: Move here: settings, blocked scripts, policy pages and visitor consent from other cookie plugins
body:
A site switching to SEO Pro Cookie Consent keeps what it set up in its old cookie plugin (settings, the scripts it blocked, its policy pages) and its visitors' existing choices. Then, with guidance, it removes the old plugin and everything it left behind. Same approach as SEO Pro Stats' "Move here" work (wpallstars/seoprostats#108), adapted to cookie plugins.

## Goal

1. **Detection by data, not just by plugin**: a source is listed whenever its data is on the site (options, tables, pages using its shortcodes or blocks), whether the plugin is active, inactive or already deleted.
2. **Import tab** (Settings → SEO Pro Cookie Consent → Import): for each source, a dry run (settings that would change, scripts and services it blocked, pages that use its documents, consent cookie it set), then import, and undo per import.
3. **Settings**: equivalent settings (regions, banner position and message, consent lifetime, policy page, Consent Mode) are filled only where ours still have their defaults, shown in the dry run first.
4. **Scripts**: the source's own blocked-script and whitelist entries go into Also hold back and Never hold back; services it lists that we already recognise are noted, not duplicated.
5. **Visitors are not asked again**: a visitor who already chose in the old banner keeps that choice. The browser reads the source's consent cookie once, maps its categories to ours, and writes `spcc_consent`, only when the source recorded an explicit choice.
6. **Policy pages keep working**: a page that shows the old plugin's cookie list gets the Cookie policy block instead; other generated documents (privacy statement, terms, imprint) are frozen as editable blocks, so nothing goes blank when the old plugin is deleted.
7. **Guided removal**: after an import, the owner checks the banner and pages, deactivates and deletes the plugin (with its own delete-data setting turned on first if it has one), or uses **Remove leftover data** once it is inactive or gone.
8. **Plugins screen and notices**: while a source has data that is not imported, or leftovers remain, a notice and a note on its row say what to do next.

## Decisions (carried over from SEO Pro Stats; change only with the owner's say)

- **One banner at a time.** Unlike statistics, cookie banners cannot run side by side. Every source plugin goes in the consent feature's `REPLACES` (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`), so our banner and blocking wait while it is active, as Complianz does today. The import runs while the source is still active; deactivating it is what switches visitors over.
- **Remove leftovers on request.** SEO Pro Cookie Consent may delete another plugin's leftover tables and options, but only through the explicit, confirmed Remove leftover data action, and only once that plugin is inactive or deleted. This is a plugin-own exception to `STANDARDS.md` → Structure, recorded in `AGENTS.md`. Imports themselves only read, except pages the owner chooses to convert.
- **Consent carry-over is conservative**: only explicit choices map across; anything unclear asks again.

## Children

Every child after the first is blocked by the first.

1. #11: engine, Import tab, consent carry-over, policy page hand-over, Remove leftover data, WP-CLI, and Complianz (free, Premium, Terms & Conditions). `tier:thinking`
2. #12: Plugins screen and admin notices through the whole cycle. `tier:standard`
3. #13: CookieYes and Cookie Notice & Compliance. `tier:standard`
4. #14: CookieAdmin, GDPR Cookie Compliance and WPConsent. `tier:standard`
5. #15: Real Cookie Banner. `tier:thinking`
6. #16: hosted banners: Cookiebot, iubenda and Termly. `tier:standard`

#11 is blocked by #3 (the consent engine).

Install counts from the WordPress.org API (October 2026): CookieYes 1M+, Complianz 1M+, Cookie Notice 800k+, CookieAdmin 400k+, GDPR Cookie Compliance 300k+, WPConsent 200k+, iubenda 200k+, Real Cookie Banner 100k+, Cookiebot 100k+, Termly 80k+. Smaller plugins (SureCookie, Cookiez, Beautiful Cookie Consent Banner and others) can follow through the `seoprocookieconsent_migrate_sources` filter or later children. Borlabs Cookie is sold outside WordPress.org; add it only with a licence for testing.

## Rules every child follows

- **Visitor pages pay nothing**: detection, import and cleanup run only in wp-admin, WP-CLI or REST. Cache detection in a non-autoloaded option, refreshed when the Import tab or Plugins screen opens. The only front-end part is the consent carry-over in `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: a cookie read, no request.
- **Imports only read** another plugin's data. The only writes are Remove leftover data (confirmed, deletes exactly what it lists, refused while that plugin is active) and page conversion the owner confirms (a revision is kept).
- **Never copy consent records** (IP addresses, user IDs) from a source's log tables; they belong to the old plugin's records and stay until the owner removes them.
- **Verify each source on a real install** of its current version (`scripts/test-site.sh up`, `scripts/test-site.sh wp plugin install <slug> --activate`, set it up, accept and reject in a browser). List its options with `wp option list --search='<prefix>*'`, its tables with `SHOW TABLES`, its cookies from the browser, and name the versions checked in the adapter's docblock. **Verify plugin slugs** with the WordPress.org plugin API.
- **Write as if public**: describe the plugins we import from in our own words, and never copy their code.
- Each source added to `REPLACES` changes the README's replaced-plugins line: run `php scripts/replaced-plugins.php --write`.

## Verification (each child)

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- On a test site with the source set up (banner position, a custom blocked script, a cookie policy page) and a visitor who accepted statistics only: the dry run lists them; import fills our settings and Also hold back; the policy page shows our block; after deactivating the source, the same visitor sees no banner and statistics only is allowed; a second import changes nothing; undo restores our settings; Remove leftover data deletes exactly the listed items and the notice goes away.

title: Move here 1: import engine, Import tab, consent carry-over, policy pages, leftovers, and Complianz
body:
Parent: #10. Read it first for the goal, the decisions and the rules. This is the first child: the engine, the Import tab, consent carry-over, policy page hand-over, Remove leftover data, and the first source, Complianz (free, Premium, Terms & Conditions). Every other child adds an adapter on top of it.

blocked-by: #3 (the consent engine must be merged first)

## Goal

1. The owner opens Settings → SEO Pro Cookie Consent → **Import** and sees Complianz listed whenever its data is on the site, with what can come across.
2. A dry run lists settings, blocked scripts, pages and the consent cookie mapping; import applies them; the Consent card reflects them.
3. The tab then asks the owner to check the banner and pages, deactivate and delete Complianz, and finally offers **Remove leftover data**.

## Design

### Source adapters

An abstract `SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate_Source`:

- `KEY`, `NAME`, `SLUGS` (plugin folders, free and Pro).
- `detect()`: whether its data is present (options, tables, pages with its shortcodes or blocks), plugin state (active, inactive, not installed). Cheap: known option names and one `SHOW TABLES LIKE`, no content scans beyond a `post_content LIKE` on its shortcode names, limited and cached.
- `settings()`: its options mapped to our setting keys, each with a converter (regions, banner position, message, consent days, policy page, Consent Mode).
- `scripts()`: the scripts it was told to block or allow, as host or path fragments for Also hold back (`category:` prefix when not marketing) and Never hold back.
- `pages()`: pages using its documents: for each, which shortcodes or blocks, and whether each is a cookie list (replace with our Cookie policy block) or another generated document (freeze as static blocks).
- `consent_cookie()`: for the browser: cookie names, how to read an explicit choice, and the category map to ours (`preferences`, `statistics`, `embeds`, `marketing`). Return nothing when the source's cookie cannot be read reliably.
- `leftovers()`: exactly what it leaves: tables (with `$wpdb->prefix`), options (known names or a prefix only it uses, checked on a real install), cron hooks, transients, user meta, upload folders, and pages it created that no longer have content. Only what is present.
- `uninstall_setting()`: its own delete-data-on-uninstall option, if any.

Registry `SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate::sources()`, extended by one class per adapter, plus a `seoprocookieconsent_migrate_sources` filter.

### Import and undo

- Settings go through `import_setting()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-feature.php`), so only defaults are filled. Move the current one-off Complianz import (`SEOProCookieConsent_Consent::migrate()`) into the Complianz adapter, so there is one path.
- Each run stores a record (non-autoloaded option `seoprocookieconsent_imports`): source, time, our settings before, the lines added to Also/Never hold back, pages converted with their revision IDs. **Undo** restores our settings and lines from it and restores page revisions.
- A second run with nothing new changes nothing.

### Consent carry-over

- The front config gets `migrate` entries from adapters whose source data is still present or was imported (only `consent_cookie()` data, a few bytes; none once the owner removes leftovers or turns it off).
- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: when there is no `spcc_consent`, read the source cookie, map an explicit choice to our categories, write `spcc_consent` with `m` from the current model and a `src` key naming the source, then continue as usual. Never treat "banner dismissed" or implied consent as opt-in consent in an opt-in place.
- Only while our feature is running (the source is inactive), so the two never race.

### Policy page hand-over

- The dry run lists each page and what would change. On import (per page, confirmed), replace the cookie list shortcode or block with the Cookie policy block, and replace other generated documents with their rendered HTML in Custom HTML or paragraph blocks, rendered while the source is still active. Keep a revision.
- If the source is already inactive, its shortcodes cannot render: offer only the cookie list replacement and say which documents need rewriting.

### Remove leftover data

`SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate::cleanup($source, $dry_run)`: lists `leftovers()`, deletes exactly that list after confirmation (tab) or `--yes` (WP-CLI). Refused while the plugin is active on this site or network-wide; needs `delete_plugins` and `manage_options`. `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS %i` per listed table, `delete_option()`, `wp_clear_scheduled_hook()`. Multisite: this site only; list network-wide leftovers without deleting. Cannot be undone: the confirmation says so and suggests a backup. Add the one-line exception to `AGENTS.md`.

### Complianz adapter

Verify on a real install of the current Complianz (free) and, if available, Premium and Complianz Terms & Conditions; name versions in the docblock. Expected, to confirm: settings in `cmplz_options` and related `cmplz_*` options; custom blocked scripts and whitelist in its script centre; documents via `[cmplz-document]` shortcodes and its blocks (cookie statement, privacy statement, imprint), and `[cmplz-terms-conditions]` from Terms & Conditions; consent cookies `cmplz_*` per category plus a banner status cookie; tables `cmplz_*`. Add `complianz-terms-conditions` to `REPLACES` only if our Terms feature (#4) exists; otherwise just freeze its page.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate.php`
- NEW: `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-source.php`

title: Consent records: keep a snapshot of the banner and policy each record was given under
body:
Follows #6 (consent records).

## Goal

Each consent record should show what the visitor was shown when they chose. Today a record keeps only the free-text `consent_policy_version` label (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php:168-174`, saved at `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:140`). The label's own description says it "does not keep a copy of the policy text". If the banner or policy text changes, an old record no longer shows what was agreed to.

## Design

- New private table `{prefix}seoprocookieconsent_snapshots`: `id`, `hash char(64)` (sha256 of the canonical JSON, unique key), `created_at`, `content longtext` (JSON: banner message, button labels, category names and descriptions, service list per category, policy page URL, the policy page's `post_modified_gmt` and revision ID, plugin version).
- Build the snapshot in PHP from the same values the banner renders (`includes/views/consent-banner.php`, the localized config at `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php:340-352`). Store a row only when the hash is new: on settings save (`SEOProCookieConsent_Settings::option_updated()`, `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-settings.php:301`), on policy page save, and lazily in `SEOProCookieConsent_Records::sync()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:43`) if none exists. Never on a visitor request.
- Send the current snapshot hash to the browser in the config (next to `'policy'` at line 350). `save()` in `assets/js/spcc.js:213-247` adds it to the record payload. `record()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:105-146`) validates it as `/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/` and stores it in a new `snapshot char(64)` column. Raise the schema version so `sync()` runs `dbDelta` again (the `SCHEMA` option now stores `'1'`). Treat a missing or unknown hash as empty, not as an error, so cached pages with an older config still record.
- CSV export (`export()`, line 176) gains a `Snapshot` column. Add a second export link for the snapshots table.
- Cleanup: never delete a snapshot that a kept record still points to.
- Wording: "evidence of what was shown". Never "proof" or "legally valid".

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`
- EDIT: `assets/js/spcc.js`
- EDIT: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`
- `uninstall.php`
- `docs/architecture.md`

Integration evidence: the new private table must be removed by the existing per-site uninstall routine (`uninstall.php`), and the architecture's Optional consent records section currently states that policy text is not archived. These plugin-owned adjacent files are necessary to keep uninstall and storage documentation correct. No shared settings/core file changes are needed: the existing `seoprocookieconsent_settings_changed` hook supplies settings-save integration. Verification includes the existing lint, smoke-test (including uninstall), Plugin Check and disposable site commands below. Collision discovery found no open related PR or competing claim on these paths; issue #41 remains assigned and in progress.

## Reference pattern

The lazy schema and append-only insert in `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:43-67` and `:131-145`.

## Acceptance

- Turning records on and making a choice stores one record with a snapshot hash, and the matching snapshot row exists.
- Changing the banner message creates exactly one new snapshot. Saving with no change creates none.
- A record sent without a hash (an old cached page) is still stored.
- Both exports open in a spreadsheet. Formula protection is kept.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- `scripts/test-site.sh up`, turn records on, choose as a visitor, change the message, choose again, export both CSVs and compare the hashes.

title: Consent records: own retention period, separate from choice lifetime
body:
Follows #6 (consent records).

## Goal

Keep consent records for their own period, separate from how long the browser remembers a choice. Today `cutoff()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:148-151`) uses `consent_days` (30-395 days), so a record is deleted when the choice it documents expires. Owners often need evidence for longer than that, for example for the time allowed to raise a complaint.

## Design

- New setting `consent_records_days` in `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php` after `consent_policy_version` (lines 168-174): `type => int`, `parent => self::KEY`, `default => 0`, `min => 0`, `max => 3650`. Label: "Keep records for (days)". Description: "0 keeps them as long as visitors' choices. Set this to how long you need evidence of consent. Records older than this are deleted." Follow the shape of `consent_days` (lines 175-184).
- `cutoff()`: when the new value is greater than 0, use `max(consent_days, consent_records_days)`. Otherwise keep the current behaviour. Never delete a record before its choice has expired.
- Update the `consent_records` description at line 166 so it no longer says "for the same lifetime as choices".
- Add the setting to the sanitize/schema tests if `scripts/smoke-test.sh` lists settings.

## Acceptance

title: Consent records: show visitors their consent ID and let admins look one up
body:
Follows #6 (consent records).

## Goal

A visitor can see their consent ID, and an administrator can look it up. Then a question like "what did I agree to?" or a regulator's request can be answered for one person. Today the anonymous ID exists only in the `spcc_consent` cookie (`assets/js/spcc.js:219-229`). The only way in for an admin is the full CSV export (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:176`).

## Design

- Visitor: when records are on and a choice has an ID, the Cookie settings dialog (`includes/views/consent-banner.php`, near `spcc-dialog__actions` at line 70) shows a small line, "Your consent ID: abcd…", with a copy button. JS fills it from `spcc.choice.id` when the dialog opens (`open()`, `assets/js/spcc.js:332`). The PHP never prints the ID, so cached pages stay safe. The line is hidden when records are off.
- Admin: next to the export button in `panel()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:167-173`), add a "Look up a consent ID" field. It posts to a new `admin_post_seoprocookieconsent_records_lookup` action: check `manage_options` and a nonce, accept only `/^[a-f0-9]{32}$/`, then use one prepared `SELECT` on `visitor_id` to show that ID's rows (time, choice, policy version, and snapshot hash once the snapshots issue lands) in an admin table, newest first. Never add a public read endpoint.
- Make sure WordPress's personal data export/erase tools are not wrongly claimed to cover these IDs. Say in `readme.txt` that the records are pseudonymous.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/views/consent-banner.php`
- EDIT: `assets/js/spcc.js`
- EDIT: `assets/css/` (the consent stylesheet that styles `.spcc-dialog__actions`)
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`
- `DESIGN.md`

Integration scope recovery: DESIGN.md records the new consent-ID row, wrapping and accessible copy feedback required by the repository UI guidance. No open PR overlaps these paths; current assigned worker owns implementation. Verify with the issue commands and desktop/mobile light/dark browser checks.

## Reference pattern

`export()` in `includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-records.php:176-214`, for the capability, nonce and prepared query.

## Acceptance

- With records on, after a choice, the dialog shows the same ID as the cookie. The copy button works with a keyboard and a screen reader.
- With records off, nothing is shown.
- The admin lookup returns that ID's rows. A malformed ID is refused, and a user without `manage_options` gets a 403.

title: Move here: turn on consent records when the source plugin kept them
body:
Follows #6 (consent records) and #10 (Move here).

## Goal

When the source plugin kept consent records on the site, the import should turn on **Keep consent records**, so records continue without a gap. Today the import only adds a note telling the owner to turn it on (for example `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-borlabs.php:135`, `-ct-gdpr.php:102`, `-real-cookie-banner.php:98`, `-source.php:238`). On a real switch (Complianz Premium with `cmplz_statistics` on augustawards.com, 2026-10-17), `consent_records` stayed `false` after the import.

## Design

- Each adapter's `settings()` sets `$result['consent_records'] = true` only when it finds evidence of site-local records: Complianz Premium's `{prefix}cmplz_statistics` table has rows (`-complianz.php:230-233` already names it), the Borlabs, Ultimate GDPR, Real Cookie Banner, CookieAdmin and WPConsent record tables (their `leftovers()` `'kept'` lists), or the source setting that turned records on. Use one `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` per table. Never read record contents.
- Hosted providers (Cookiebot, iubenda, Termly) keep their records off-site. Leave the setting unchanged and keep their current note.
- The value goes through the normal import plan, so the dry run lists it and undo restores it (`includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate.php:285-312`, `:336-371`). If the owner has turned records on or off themselves since then, keep their choice, following the existing "changed since" check at line 352.
- Change the matching notes from "turn on Keep consent records" to "Keep consent records was turned on to continue its records".

title: Work with consent automation (autoconsent, Consent-O-Matic): stable hooks and rules
body:
## Goal

Visitors who use consent automation (DuckDuckGo's autoconsent, built into the DuckDuckGo browser and used by other extensions, and Consent-O-Matic) should have their stored preference applied to our banner through its real controls. That choice is then saved, honoured by the blocker, and recorded like any other choice. This is the opposite of hiding the banner from such tools: they should find it, understand it and answer it correctly. Treat refusals and partial choices as fully as accepts.

Context: this came up for CookiesClerk on 2026-10-17. Its Chrome Web Store listing describes a cookie/account switcher, not a banner answerer, so no CookiesClerk work is needed. The two tools above are the ones that answer banners.

## Problem space

- Both tools match banners with per-CMP rules: CSS selectors to detect the banner, open the settings, toggle categories, save and confirm. Rules are maintained upstream (DuckDuckGo `autoconsent` rules and Consent-O-Matic's rule list). Read each project's rule format and contribution guide; do not guess repository paths.
- Our markup: `includes/views/consent-banner.php` (ids `spcc-banner`, `spcc-dialog`, `.spcc-dialog__actions` at line 70). Behaviour is in `assets/js/spcc.js` (`save()` at 213, `open()` at 332, `close()` at 365). The choice cookie is `spcc_consent` (JSON, `m: opt-in|opt-out`).
- Decide which stable hooks to commit to, for example `data-spcc-action="accept-all|reject-all|save"` and `data-spcc-category="statistics"` on the toggles. Add them to `DESIGN.md` or the developer docs as a public contract so later markup changes do not break the rules.
- Decide whether to offer a small public JS API (for example `window.spcc.set({statistics:0, marketing:0})`) that rules can call instead of clicking. Weigh this against rule authors preferring plain DOM steps.
- Self-test: add the rule locally to an autoconsent checkout and run its test harness against `scripts/test-site.sh up`. Confirm opt-out leaves every optional category off and records `m: opt-in` (an explicit choice, not a dismissal).
- Record evidence: think about whether records should mark automated answers. This is likely not detectable or desirable; write down the decision.

## Deliverables

1. Stable hooks in the markup, plus documentation.
2. Draft rules for autoconsent and Consent-O-Matic, kept in `docs/` or `tests/` in this repo, with the local test results.
3. Upstream PRs to both projects once the plugin is public, or a recorded reason for waiting (the repo is private today, and upstream rules usually need a live public example site).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/views/consent-banner.php`
- EDIT: `assets/js/spcc.js`
- EDIT: `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`
- NEW: rule drafts under `docs/consent-automation/` (directory to create)

title: Ask for consent when a clicked video or map needs a held-back Embeds service
body:
## Problem

On augustawards.com (Kadence video popups, 2026-10-17), clicking a video before Embeds is allowed opens an empty lightbox. Kadence's GLightbox loads Plyr, and Plyr loads `https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api`. `hold()` in `assets/js/spcc-head.js:289-321` holds that script as YouTube (Embeds). Because it is a script, not an iframe, there is no placeholder (`placeholder()`, line 418, handles iframes only). The visitor is never told why the video is blank.

## Fix

- `assets/js/spcc-head.js`: record the time of the last trusted `pointerdown`/`keydown`/`touchstart` (capture phase). When `hold()` holds a script or iframe in the `embeds` category within a few seconds of that gesture, and it was not held before, call `spcc.ask(id, category)` asynchronously. The page loading on its own never asks.
- `assets/js/spcc.js`: `spcc.ask()` opens Cookie settings (`open()`) with a note: "{service} needs {category} to show here." It does not pre-tick anything. The existing Accept all / Save choices release the held script (`release()`), and the player builds. It asks at most once per service per page and never while the dialog is open.
- `includes/views/consent-banner.php`: a hidden note element in the dialog. `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`: the translatable note text in the config `text`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/smoke-test.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`
- On the test site: a Kadence video popup with a YouTube URL. Click it with no choice: the dialog opens with the note. Accept all: the video plays. Reload with Embeds rejected and click again: the dialog opens again. Loading a page with no clicks never opens the dialog.

title: Cookie settings preset on the Menus screen and smarter footer placement
body:
## What

1. **Menus screen preset:** add a "Cookie settings" box to Appearance → Menus, so owners can tick it and add a `#cookie-settings` link without knowing the anchor or building a custom link. Show it by default (WordPress hides new menu boxes for users who have never saved Screen Options).
2. **Smarter automatic footer link** (`consent_menu_link`): place it right after the cookie policy page link, or else right before the privacy policy link, in any footer menu; fall back to the end of the theme's footer-location menu as today.

## Why

On a live site (Kadence, footer menus shown through Navigation Menu widgets) the automatic link never appeared: `SEOProCookieConsent_Consent::menu_link()` only matches `$args->theme_location` in `FOOTER_LOCATIONS`, and widget menus have no location. The owner had to add a custom `#cookie-settings` link by hand under Cookie Policy.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-consent.php`:
  - Footer menus = menus assigned to a `FOOTER_LOCATIONS` location, or whose name contains "footer" (covers widget/block-rendered classic menus via `$args->menu`).
  - Work out one target per request: first footer menu with the cookie policy page (`consent_policy_url` → page, by object ID or URL) → after it; else first with the privacy page (`wp_page_for_privacy_policy`) → before it; else append to footer-location menus (current behaviour).
  - Mark the reference item in `wp_nav_menu_objects`, then insert the `<li>` beside it in `wp_nav_menu_items` and strip the marker. Skip if the reference item has a submenu (append instead).
  - Skip entirely when any saved menu item already links to `#cookie-settings` (owner placed it).
  - Match the neighbour's Title Case for the English label ("Cookie Settings" next to "Cookie Policy").
- New nav-menus meta box using core's `.posttypediv` / `.categorychecklist` markup (`menu-item[-1][menu-item-type]=custom`, URL `#cookie-settings`) so `nav-menu.js` `addSelectedToMenu` handles it; unhide once per user on first visit.

## Verification

- `composer`/project lint (`php -l`, PHPCS as configured).
- Local WP: Appearance → Menus shows the box; Add to Menu creates a custom link `#cookie-settings`.
- Front end with a widget-rendered footer menu holding Cookie Policy: the link appears directly after it; with only Privacy Policy, directly before it; with a saved `#cookie-settings` item, no automatic link.

"Remove leftover data" after a Complianz or Real Cookie Banner import misses some source-owned data. Checked on a live site after both sources were imported, cleaned up and deleted:

| Left behind | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Post meta `_cmplz_scanned_post` (973), `_cmplz_remote_scanned_post` (257), `cmplz_hide_cookiebanner` (548, all empty) | Complianz | Scanner bookkeeping and the per-page "hide banner" toggle |

| Option `external_updates-real-cookie-banner-pro` | Real Cookie Banner | Update-checker state keyed by its slug |

Correctly kept: empty `wp_cmplz_statistics` and `wp_cmplz_dnsmpd` (records), by design. Not ours to remove: Admin Columns' `_ac_columns_default_cmplz-*` options.

## How

- `includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate.php` `cleanup()`: support two new removable kinds, `meta` (post meta keys, `delete_post_meta_by_key`) and `files` (directories under uploads, removed with `WP_Filesystem`, path confirmed inside `wp_upload_dir()['basedir']`). Add both to `REMOVABLE`.
- `class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-complianz.php` `leftovers()`: list the three meta keys when present, and the generated upload subfolders present; keep `uploads/complianz/snapshots` (Premium proof-of-consent PDFs) as `kept`.
- `class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate-real-cookie-banner.php` `leftovers()`: add `external_updates-real-cookie-banner` / `-pro`.

title: Import stops when a page's newest revision is an autosave
body:
## What happens

`wp seoprocookieconsent migrate import complianz --pages=...` (and the Import tab) stops with "A page revision could not be saved. Nothing was replaced." when a selected page's newest revision is an autosave.

Seen on a production Complianz site: page 1055's revisions, newest first, were `1055-autosave-v1` (2024, content differs), then `1055-revision-v1` (content matches the page).

## Why

`SEOProCookieConsent_Migrate::revision()` (`includes/migrate/class-seoprocookieconsent-migrate.php`) calls `wp_save_post_revision()`. Core finds the page unchanged since its newest *real* revision (it skips autosaves) and returns null. The fallback then takes the newest entry from `wp_get_post_revisions()`, which here is the autosave, so the content check fails and it returns 0.

## Fix

In the fallback, skip autosaves (`wp_is_post_autosave()`) and compare the newest real revision, as core does. Undo then restores that real revision.

## Verification

- `php -l`, project lint (`composer lint` / CI Lint PHP 7.4).
- On the affected site, rerun the import for the same pages after deploying: the import completes with `changed: true`, and the undo record points at the `-revision-v1` revision.

## What happens

The import replaces a source cookie policy (Complianz cookie statement, `[cookie_audit]`, `[rcb-cookie-policy]` and so on) with `<!-- wp:seoprocookieconsent/cookie-policy /-->`, but leaves the **Cookie policy** feature (`policy`) off. `SEOProCookieConsent_Policy::boot()` (`includes/features/class-seoprocookieconsent-policy.php`) registers the block and shortcode only when the feature is on, so the page renders its heading and no cookie list until someone turns the feature on by hand. title: Embed placeholders shrink to 100px for percentage-sized iframes; maps get a generic map image
body:
## What happens

A held-back iframe sized in percentages (`width="100%" height="100%"`) gets a 100px-square placeholder. Kadence's Google Maps block (`.kb-google-maps-container`) uses those percentages, and its container sets the height. So a migrated directory listing shows a tiny box with an unreadable notice where the map should be.

Cause: `SEOProCookieConsent_Blocker::iframe()` (`includes/class-seoprocookieconsent-blocker.php`) casts the attributes with `(int)`, so `"100%"` becomes `100` and the placeholder gets `aspect-ratio:100/100;max-width:100px`. `placeholder()` in `assets/js/spcc-head.js` has the same bug through `parseInt`.

Maps also show only a plain tint. Complianz shows a generic map image under the notice, which looks more like the content that will load.

## Fix

- Copy the iframe's width and height into the placeholder only when they're pixels, as aspect ratio and max width (PHP and JS). When they're percentages, copy them as `width`/`height` so the placeholder fills the same container.
- For map services (`'embed' => 'map'`, currently Google Maps), show a bundled generic map SVG (`assets/images/map-placeholder.svg`) as `.spcc-embed__thumbnail`. It reuses the existing scrim behind the notice. It's served from the plugin, so nothing reaches Google before consent.
- Note the map image in `DESIGN.md` → Front end and `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verification

- `composer lint` / the project's checks pass.
- Deploy to the reported Property Services Directory listing. Before consent, the placeholder fills the Kadence map container and shows the map image and a readable notice. Load map shows the map.

body:
## Task


Every fleet script that changes plugin state on a host must snapshot the
stored `active_plugins` before the change, check it afterwards, and stop with
a FAIL line and a restore command when anything other than the intended
change happened. It must also stop when WP-CLI reports a database connection
error.

Two deliverables:

1. `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()`: guard the
`wp plugin install --force` step (it keeps activation, so the active list
must be identical before and after).
2. A repository-owned migration rollout, `scripts/migrate-sites.sh` plus
`scripts/lib/migrate-remote.sh`. These replace the ad hoc host-side script
used on 2026-10-17, which is not in any repository. Model them on
`deploy-sites.sh` and `deploy-remote.sh`, and run every activate or
deactivate through the same guard.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `marcusquinn.com hostinger wordpress plugins deactivated` → 0 prior hits; incident lesson stored this session
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` or `RELEASING.md` in the last 48h
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked at `origin/main` a739711 (`scripts/deploy-sites.sh`, `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()`, `RELEASING.md:22`, `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php` `stored_plugins()`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — reference pattern exists; worker decides helper shape and exact WP-CLI calls
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — no code drafted; the brief carries the evidence

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-18
- **Session:** opencode:interactive (marcusquinn.com incident review)
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Target repository:** wpallstars/seoprocookieconsent
- **Conversation context:** All plugins on one fleet site were left inactive during the Complianz → SEO Pro Cookie Consent rollout on 2026-10-17. The owner asked for the fleet tooling to guard against this.

## What

Every fleet script that changes plugin state on a host must snapshot the
stored `active_plugins` before the change, check it afterwards, and stop with
a FAIL line and a restore command when anything other than the intended
change happened. It must also stop when WP-CLI reports a database connection
error.

Two deliverables:

1. `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()`: guard the
   `wp plugin install --force` step (it keeps activation, so the active list
   must be identical before and after).
2. A repository-owned migration rollout, `scripts/migrate-sites.sh` plus
   `scripts/lib/migrate-remote.sh`. These replace the ad hoc host-side script
   used on 2026-10-17, which is not in any repository. Model them on
   `deploy-sites.sh` and `deploy-remote.sh`, and run every activate or
   deactivate through the same guard.

## Why

Incident on 2026-10-17 (UTC):

- At 21:03:14, the ad hoc migration ran `wp plugin activate seoprocookieconsent` on a site whose MySQL connection was failing. WP-CLI printed `Error: Error establishing a database connection.`, and the site's PHP log had `Commands out of sync` errors at the same time.
- Core's `activate_plugin()` read `active_plugins` as empty and saved `["seoprocookieconsent/seoprocookieconsent.php"]`. The other 54 plugins were deactivated.
- The script carried on: it imported, deactivated the source plugins and deleted them. Nothing compared the active list, so the site ran without its plugins for about 100 minutes until someone noticed.
- The site was recovered by hand from an older database dump.
- 12 other sites in the same run were fine. The failure is intermittent and depends on the database state, so it needs a hard guard, not more care.

## Tier

### Tier checklist (verify before assigning)

- [ ] **Exact execution contract supplied?** No: the helper shape and the WP-CLI calls are left to the worker.
- [x] **Targets and reference pattern verified?**
- [ ] **No semantic or design decision remains?** The worker decides the restore-versus-stop policy for multisite networks.
- [x] **Bounded, reversible, low-consequence impact?** These are operator scripts, not the plugin runtime.
- [x] **No stateful coordination to invent?**
- [x] **Focused verification and rollback are explicit?**
- [x] **No dispatch-path risk override?**

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a known pattern (`deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()` FAIL lines with restore commands) applied to a new guard and a new script, with a few implementation choices left to the worker.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task: use a normal closing keyword for this issue.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
wp --path="$root" --skip-plugins --skip-themes eval 'global $wpdb; echo $wpdb->get_var("SELECT option_value FROM {$wpdb->options} WHERE option_name = \"active_plugins\"");'
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` — add `active_snapshot ROOT` (prints the sorted raw list, fails on a database error) and `active_check ROOT BEFORE EXPECTED_ADD EXPECTED_REMOVE`; call them around the install in `apply_one()`.
- `NEW: scripts/migrate-sites.sh` — local wrapper modelled on `scripts/deploy-sites.sh`: `--host`, `--tag`, `--source complianz|...`, `--parent`, `--skip`, `--dry-run` by default, `--apply`. It downloads and checks the zip the same way.
- `NEW: scripts/lib/migrate-remote.sh` — remote part. Per install: database backup (mysqldump with a `--defaults-extra-file` mode-600 config) plus a tar of the source plugin folders; install if missing; guarded activate; `wp seoprocookieconsent migrate plan <source>`; `migrate import <source> --pages=<renderable ids>`; turn on `consent`, and `policy` when imported policy blocks exist; guarded deactivate of the source plugins; verify the home page returns 200 and the banner is present. - `EDIT: RELEASING.md` — document `migrate-sites.sh` next to the `deploy-sites.sh` row (line 22), including the active-list guard.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` streams or copies `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`; the new wrapper does the same for `migrate-remote.sh`. No PHP caller.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the remote scripts' WP-CLI calls (`plugin install --force`, `plugin activate`, `plugin deactivate`, `eval delete_plugins`); the guard's restore writes `active_plugins` with `update_option()` while option filters are paused (same approach as `without_list_filters()`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/lint.sh` (ShellCheck); `scripts/test-site.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` give a local Docker WordPress for exercising the remote parts.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A. No plugin options change; the guard only reads and restores the core `active_plugins` and `active_sitewide_plugins` options.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** N/A. The scripts are not part of the release zip; check that `scripts/build-release.sh` keeps excluding `scripts/`.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A for data. This is a new operator workflow only.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** print a restore command on every FAIL; the migration backup folder lives in `~/.seoprocookieconsent-deploy/migrate-<name>-<stamp>` (mode 700), as in the existing deploy layout.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the snapshot helper. Read the raw option with `$wpdb`, unserialize it, and print the sorted plugin files one per line. Treat as a hard failure: WP-CLI output containing `Error establishing a database connection`, a non-zero exit, or a value that is not an array. An empty array counts as valid only when the site really has no active plugins, so record the count as well.
2. Add the check helper. Compute the expected list (before + add − remove) and compare it with a fresh snapshot. On mismatch: print FAIL with the missing and extra entries, restore the before list (with the multisite policy decided and documented in the script header), re-check, set FAILED=1 and skip all later steps for that install.
3. Wire the guard into `deploy-remote.sh` `apply_one()` with expected add/remove both empty.
4. Write `migrate-remote.sh` and `migrate-sites.sh` as in Files to Modify. Guard every plugin state change, and stop the install on the first FAIL; do not go on to import, deactivate or delete.
5. Update `RELEASING.md`, then run `scripts/lint.sh`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** something else on the site (cron, a visitor in wp-admin) can change `active_plugins` between the snapshot and the check. Report that as a FAIL with a diff, never silently overwrite, and restore only when the stored list is a strict subset of the before list (a wipe).
- **Migration/rollback:** the database backup is taken before any change, and the restore command must be printed.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** deploy-remote.sh output keeps its existing columns; the guard adds a FAIL reason only.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a rerun must skip installs whose source plugins are already gone and whose import record exists (`seoprocookieconsent_imports` option).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** each install is independent; one FAIL never stops the whole host run, but it stops every later step for that install.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `apply_one` in `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- **Current line count:** about 60 lines
- **Estimated growth:** +10 lines if the helpers stay separate functions
- **Projected post-change:** about 70 lines

```bash
bash scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh list seoprocookieconsent '<docroot pattern>'
```

- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** no plugin PHP runtime changes; never run `--apply` against production hosts from the worker. Production rollout remains an operator step.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (interactive session).

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh`
- `scripts/migrate-sites.sh`

- `RELEASING.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a plugin activate, deactivate or install leaves `active_plugins` with entries missing, or WP-CLI reports a database connection error, the install prints FAIL with the diff and a restore command, the list is restored, and no later step (import, deactivate, delete) runs for that install.

title: fix: consent buttons fail text contrast in Kadence dark mode
body:
## What

Consent buttons (banner Accept/Reject, Cookie settings Save, embed placeholder "Load …") fail text contrast in Kadence dark mode.

## Evidence

Live Kadence Pro site, `body.color-switch-dark` (Kadence dark mode switcher):

- `--global-palette-btn` resolves to palette 9 (`#1a202c`) and `--global-palette-btn-bg` to palette 1 (`#c00d10`).
- `.spcc-btn` and `.spcc-embed__load` inherit both: `rgb(26, 32, 44)` on `rgb(192, 13, 16)` = **2.57:1** (WCAG AA needs 4.5:1).
- Kadence's own header button stays readable (`#fff` on `#c00d10`, 6.35:1) only because it has its own colour setting.
- Hover pair has the same problem (`--global-palette-btn-hover` = palette 9 on palette 2).

Light mode passes (`#fff` on `#0e0995`).

## Fix

CSS cannot reliably compute contrast across browsers yet (`contrast-color()` support is incomplete), so `assets/js/spcc.js` checks the resolved theme pair at runtime:

- Keep the theme's button text when it reaches 4.5:1.
- Otherwise use the theme's own light/dark text (`--spcc-bg` / `--spcc-strong`, i.e. palette 9 / 3) with the higher contrast, then `#fff` / `#000` as a last resort.
- Do the same for the hover pair.
- Publish the result as `--spcc-btn-ink` / `--spcc-btn-ink-hover` on `<body>` (inherits into banner, dialog and dynamically added placeholders); CSS uses `var(--spcc-btn-ink, var(--spcc-btn-text))`.
- Re-check when `<body>` class/style changes (Kadence switcher) and on `prefers-color-scheme` changes (block themes).

### Files Scope

- `assets/js/spcc.js`
- `assets/css/spcc.css`
- `DESIGN.md`
- `STYLING.md`

## Verification

- Kadence page, light mode: buttons unchanged (theme text kept).
- Swap body class to `color-switch-dark`: button text ≥ 4.5:1 on normal and hover; no console errors.
- Theme without palette (fallbacks): unchanged.
